result.title: CityDeploy-Bench: Benchmarking Physics-Grounded Spatial Set Planning for Multi-Transmitter Network Deployment
result.summary: Automating city-scale wireless deployment remains challenging under complex urban propagation and network-wide interference. We introduce \textbf{CityDeploy-Bench}, a benchmark that reframes multi-transmitter deployment as \emph{physics-grounded spatial set planning} under a unified ray-tracing verifier. The benchmark separates utility representation from planning dynamics, enabling controlled comparison between direct scalar rewards, relational models, and higher-order interaction structures across diverse planners. Our experiments reveal a clear transition in planning behavior as physical coupling grows. Deployment quality becomes increasingly dependent on whether the learned utility captures collective transmitter interactions, whereas stronger search alone cannot compensate for missing relational structure. This establishes multi-transmitter deployment as a coordination problem over physically interacting sets rather than a collection of independent spatial decisions. We release CityDeploy-Data and the benchmark framework as a reproducible testbed for research linking decision learning with physically grounded wireless network design.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 CityDeploy-Bench，把多发射机城市无线部署重构为「物理接地的空间集合规划」，在统一 ray-tracing 验证器下对照标量奖励、关系模型与高阶交互结构对规划行为的影响，发现物理耦合增强时部署质量取决于效用是否捕捉发射机间的集体交互，单纯加强搜索无法弥补关系结构缺失。
AI.relevance_reason: 其将效用表示与规划动态解耦、并以物理验证器做对照比较的思路，可能为 LVR 中「latent 是否保留实体关系」以及表示与推理动态的贡献分配提供实验设计线索，但领域距离较远，可迁移性待核查。
